rationale: The kind of a record declaration, found by the grammar audit rather than by reading code. The pinned tree-sitter-c_sharp grammar spells `record class Foo` AND `record struct Foo` as ONE node type — `record_declaration` — and enumerating wasm/tree-sitter-c_sharp.wasm yields 533 node types with NO `record_struct_declaration` (script/m14/tmp/f1-csharp-record-probe.ts). The lane's kind rule was `stringIncludes(type, "struct")`, which can never be true for that node, so the pre-fix behaviour was measured at this fixture's source (script/m14/tmp/cs-record-struct-probe.ts): `public record struct RS(double X, double Y);` parsed with 0 errors and published kind=class, isStruct=false, isValueType=false, while docs/analyzers/csharp.md claimed record structs produce a struct. The two forms differ by an UNNAMED TOKEN child — `*record("record") *class("class")` versus `*record("record") *struct("struct")` — so the fix reads the token (csharpTypeDeclarationKind), not the node type and not the node's text. It also replaced the dead `constraint_clause` literal with the grammar's real `type_parameter_constraints_clause` and deleted eight `record_struct_declaration` disjuncts that could never be true; that half is BEHAVIOUR-NEUTRAL on every authored shape (the real node is not a declared-type node, so the guard's outcome is the same either way) and is therefore gated by F1's dead-literal register, not by an assertion here — see the round record. Measured pre-existing behaviour this fixture deliberately does NOT pin: a record's positional parameters also produce `uses <Record> -> <Positional>` self-edges (the CS-R1 rule leaves record positionals unbound so property reads flow), which is noted as an open question with its owner rather than blessed as contract.
